question.text:
A nucleus of mass $M+\Delta m$ is at rest and decays into two daughter nuclei of equal mass $\frac{M}{2}$ each. Speed of light is $\mathrm{c}$.
40. The binding energy per nucleon for the parent nucleus is $E_1$ and that for the daughter nuclei is $E_2$. Then

solution.text: After decay, the daughter nuclei will be more stable hence binding energy per nucleon will be more than that of their parent nucleus.
